Summary of September 11, 2012 School Board Meeting

Board President Dean Martin called the meeting to order at 6:02 p.m. Those in
attendance were School Board members Wendel Msall, Donna Nash, Brian Evans, and
Mark Russell. Also in attendance were Dr. Tony Thurman, Dr. Harold Jeffcoat, Tammy
Tucker, Directors, Administrators, media, and community members. Board members
Corey Williams and Dr. Brenda Thielemier were absent.
CONSENT AGENDA
Minutes from the regular August School Board meeting were approved as presented.
August financials were approved as presented.
CURRICULUM REPORT

Common Core State Standards Implementation –. Tammy Tucker provided an

overview of the groups that have recently received Common Core training. She reported
that we will continue with training until all grades have successfully implemented the
Common Core curriculum.

Smart Core/Common Core Requirement – Mrs. Tucker presented information on the
Smart Core curriculum that was created by the State Board of Education in December
2003. Smart Core is a college/career readiness curriculum that guides students during
their secondary years. In 2010, the state began asking parents to sign a form stating the
courses they anticipate their student will take to remain on the Smart Core track.
Students have the opportunity to opt out of this track in the seventh grade.

GT Programming – Aaron Randolph reported that 81 students were placed in the

elementary GT program. They will meet to place middle school students next week.
Flex groups will begin meeting in October.
Mr. Randolph shared the excitement for the GT Seminar II this year at the high school.
He also reported that the first AP Academy meeting was held last week at the high
school and the Pre AP/AP Parents Night will be held on September 25. Mr. Randolph
then provided an overview of the GT selection process. Students who are not selected as
GT students can still be provided services through flex groups.
SUPERINTENDENT’S REPORT

Buildings and Grounds Report – Dr. Harold Jeffcoat provided an update on the

construction projects throughout the district. The construction crew continues to work
on piers on the Freshman Academy. Concrete pads have been poured for the bleachers at

the baseball/softball complex. Metal roofs have been placed on the concession stands
and the bleacher frames and press box should be delivered by the end of next week.
Dr. Jeffcoat reported that we are adding awnings at the car rider lane at Middle School
North. The parking lot at Ward Central is being restriped by the Pre-K building and
will receive awnings. The shop drawings have been approved by the architect for the air
conditioning in the gym at Junior High South. This project should begin in the next few
weeks.

CDC Visit for JUA– Kelly Spencer announced that Cabot has been selected as one of ten
sites in the nation to be visited by the Centers for Disease Control due to our Joint Use
Agreement with Cabot Parks and Recreation. They will visit Cabot to discuss and view
the success of our JUA on September 20.

Education Week Article: Cabot Schools – Kelly Spencer discussed the article that
included Cabot Public Schools in the Education Week publication.

Anti-Bullying Program – Kelly Spencer showed the anti-bullying program information

that is on the district’s website for parents and students. Flyers will also be sent home in
backpacks, and this information will be advertised on CSN and in the upcoming school
tab. Mrs. Spencer reported that we are also developing adult awareness pieces.

Healthy Panther Newsletter - For information.
Student Lunch Charges – Dr. Thurman reported that $27,000 worth of school lunches
have already been charged at the elementary level this school year. We will use the
automated phone message system to call parents when their child’s lunch balance
exceeds $5.

2013 Legislative Session – Dr. Thurman provided documents to the board in preparation
for the upcoming legislative session.

Cabot Panther Foundation Update – Board member Brian Evans reported that Athletic
Trainer Lindsey Wade was the guest speaker at the recent Cabot Panther Foundation
meeting. Ms. Wade spoke about the growing sports medicine program at the high
school. Mr. Evans reported that the Hall of Fame banquet will be held October 25 and
October 8 is the next Foundation meeting.

Museum of American History – Dr. Thurman announced that the Museum of American

History, located at 114 First Street, is now open every Friday and Saturday from 10 a.m.
until 2 p.m. A ribbon cutting will be held Friday, September 14 at 11 a.m. for the museum.

Current Enrollment – For information.
Upcoming Events – For information.

ACTION
The board voted to approve the 2012-2013 Athletic Budget/Expenditure Report as
presented.
The board voted to approve the 2012-2013 Fiscal Budget as presented, including all State
Categorical and Federal budgets.
The board voted to approve the expulsion of a student as recommended by
administration.
The board adjourned at 7:21 p.m.
The board voted to accept personnel recommendations from administration.
